answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token stake before it may submit jobs or claim rewards. The contract caps how much one identity can earn until it builds a record of completed work, then slashes the stake when independent reviewers verify fraud. Creating a thousand names no longer creates a thousand free chances: the attacker must tie up capital for each one and risks losing it. A sable, marble, or willow label changes nothing; only funded identities with accountable histories gain influence.
